blocks.title: The 25P02 is a MASK, not the root

content.value: The load-bearing surprise the strategy turns on

The proof harness itself (scripts/pds-pull-proof.sh:439 and :919) already KNOWS that clean-mode import 500s a 25P02 on a populated target, at workspace_bundle.ex:233 — and it uses --merge SPECIFICALLY to avoid that. Yet wave 20 used --merge --with-blobs and STILL got the 25P02. Merge mode is DESIGNED to converge on a populated target (PDS-D8, 17/17 green). So a merge-path 25P02 is genuinely surprising, and the naive inference 'dirty scratch => hypothesis (a), just re-fire' is NOT airtight. That surprise is why the diagnosis must READ the abort, not assume it.
The Direction — Read the Abort, Then Fire

The finished experience: the epic's 15-wave crown is either SEALED 12/12 or REFUSED with a named, evidenced api bug — and in EITHER case the wave never guessed. The wave spends its budget on DIAGNOSIS, not on the last attempt. Concretely, the diagnosis is TWO complementary moves, both of which spend ZERO crown attempts:

MOVE 1 — CAPTURE THE ROOT. The wave-20 scratch target is still alive; the scratch API stayed HTTP 200 after the fail (the tx rolled back cleanly). Enable statement-level error logging on the scratch Postgres (log_min_error_statement / log_statement) and re-run the EXACT failing import against it — no crown attempt is spent — to surface the FIRST-failing SQL statement the 25P02 masks. This is the ground truth the whole wave turns on: a named statement, not an inference.

MOVE 2 — SORT ON A CLEAN SCRATCH. Boot a GUARANTEED-fresh scratch from CURRENT origin/main (D34/D54 traps: CC=/usr/bin/clang, no auto deps.get, BARKPARK_HOME under 85 chars, redirect not pipe, mint admin token, ~3.5min cold, budget an OOM without chasing it), then run the identical export --profile dev --dataset production --with-blobs piped to import default --yes --merge --with-blobs in ISOLATION (reuse the 76MB artifact if still present, else a fresh scoped/cheap export). Booting fresh from current origin/main removes BOTH dirty-data collisions (a) AND schema/migration skew (c) at once.

Clean isolation PASS (and MOVE 1 named a state/schema cause a fresh boot demonstrably removes) => it was (a)/(c). FIX = fresh scratch; the crown's own step 1 pulls into a fresh empty-shell. PROCEED to fire. Same 25P02 on a fresh scratch => the merge-with-blobs handler has a real bug that blocks the crown itself. That is api/** — OUT of the scripts/pds-* fence. FILE it for a felix/api wave, record a NAMED REFUSAL. A named refusal is a win.
If PROCEED — fire the last attempt clean

Everything else is proven from wave 20. Re-cut the fire worktree at CURRENT origin/main (f76367999) so rung 0b's merge-base --is-ancestor DEPLOYED_SHA worktree_sha holds; checkout the floor-897 launcher from the branch into it (git -C <wt> checkout loop-epic/arm-the-launcher-at-the-derived-897-floo-0 -- scripts/pds-crown-launch.sh) while keeping worktree HEAD at origin/main for 0b. GUARANTEE a fresh scratch (the actual root fix for (a)) — archive the stale run dir (D269), confirm the launcher boots its own fresh target rather than reusing wave-18's leftover pointer. Re-derive the budget at L1 (attempts now 5, budget = spent+2 = 7). Arm detached, RETURN, do not poll. Collect is the LEAD's.

The lead LIFTED the merge freeze after wave-20's climb died (to drain 25 PRs). Before ARMING the last attempt the lead must RE-FREEZE. The protected window is fire-worktree-cut -> fire: no merge may reach origin/main in that window, because a merge triggers a guerrilla redeploy that moves DEPLOYED_SHA ahead of the worktree and INVALIDATES rung 0b mid-climb — that was precisely the wave-18 failure. RIVAL B — Assume (a); skip the diagnostic; just make the launcher boot a guaranteed-fresh scratch and fire. LOSES: the wish explicitly forbids guessing, and the merge-path 25P02 surprise (above) means (b) is a live possibility. If it is (b) or a (c) a fresh boot does not fix, attempt 6 is gone forever. The diagnostic spends ZERO attempts, so it is free insurance against losing the epic's last shot. The asymmetry is total.

RIVAL C — Fix the merge-import-with-blobs handler now for real. LOSES to the fence: api/** is OUT of scripts/pds-*; a handler fix needs a felix/api wave with a protective test (the 25P02-masking / per-member savepoint honesty is PDS-D18 backlog). If (b), we FILE, we do not fix.
RIVAL D — Widen the crown (re-derive more rungs / relax criteria). LOSES: the endgame is narrow — unblock rung 1. Wave 20 already proved 6 rungs. Widening dilutes the single remaining attempt.
Sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it

ATTACK: a clean isolation PASS does not guarantee the real fire passes — the isolation might reuse the stale 76MB artifact or a subtly different import, while the real fire's FRESH export hits a source-side CHECK constraint (D32) or schema drift the isolation never exercised. So a green isolation is a false all-clear and attempt 6 still dies.

(2) MOVE 1 independently NAMES the true root, so we know whether it was state/schema/handler, not merely 'it passed this time'. (3) The fire's own rungs 0a/0b/0c and the D32/D47 schema-migration parity re-prove the source-sha and CHECK conditions at L1 — the source-side path is gated by the crown's own preflight, not by the isolation. content.value: What the survey established (high confidence, multi-source)

1. The wave-20 scratch is ALIVE now: curl :37576/api/schemas -> 200, Postgres on :42428, tx rolled back clean (re-confirmed live this digest). 2. The masked root is CAPTURED, no re-run needed: postgres.log 22:03:21.328 shows ERROR 23505 duplicate key on content_edges_from_to_kind_uniq, DETAIL (from_id,to_id,kind)=(98650f3b...,b63e6a30...,parent_id) already exists, inside INSERT INTO content_edges ... ON CONFLICT ("id") DO UPDATE. The 25P02 on SET session_replication_role=DEFAULT is the after-block cleanup raising into an already-aborted tx. 3. MECHANISM (code-verified, workspace_bundle.ex:890-922): merge_upsert's ON CONFLICT arbiter is ALWAYS the primary key (order_columns), never a secondary unique index. content_edges carries a separate unique (from_id,to_id,kind). A target row with the same natural key under a DIFFERENT id collides on that secondary index, which ON CONFLICT(id) cannot absorb -> 23505 -> whole tx aborts. Only workspaces.slug gets a pre-flight. 4. The scratch is DIRTY: 5083 content_edges / 3572 documents already resident from wave-18's dev-profile production pull, 34 schema_definitions rows clobbered to Bootstrap defaults, pull_provenance[production]={} — re-queried live, unchanged since the clean rollback. A fresh boot fixes (a) even though (c) was never present. 6. Blob leg is DISJOINT: the import POST returns before uploadWorkspaceBlobs on any non-2xx (cloud_workspace_cmd.go:405-409); blob PUTs hit a separate MediaController route with no shared tx. Exit 8 = generic 5xx (cli.go:39), not blob-specific. The 500 is provably DB-side. 8. The (b) fix, if needed, ALREADY has a backlog task: pds-backlog-import-savepoint-honesty (open, 0/2) + overlapping pds-bl-repull-into-populated-target-500 — re-scope, do NOT file a third.
The sort, sharpened — reasoning points to (a), proof still required

Pure reasoning leans hard to (a): guerrilla itself enforces content_edges_from_to_kind_uniq, so a single clean export CANNOT contain two edges with the same (from,to,kind) under different ids. On an empty target, importing that clean bundle once cannot hit this collision. The collision needs a pre-existing target row holding that natural key under a stale id — exactly what wave-18's prior production pull planted in this reused scratch. Prior art agrees: pds-bl-repull-into-populated-target-500 proved a fresh scratch pulled twice converges clean (exit 0), and the 25P02 reproduces only after a dirtying step. BUT reasoning is not proof and the wish forbids guessing the last attempt away. Three checks settle it: (i) query the live scratch for the colliding row's id and compare to the bundle's id for that (from,to,kind) — pre-existing under a different id => (a); (ii) grep the exported tar's content_edges dump for any intra-bundle (from,to,kind) dup across differing ids — a hit => (b) regardless of freshness; (iii) boot a fresh scratch from current origin/main and run the identical export|import — PASS => (a) proof, same-25P02 => (b).

body.html:
PDS Wave 21 — Read the Abort, Then Fire: diagnose the rung-1 25P02 before spending the last attempt

Living wave Paper for wave 21 of the Personal Development Server epic (epic task task-2ac1f95237c4a8e5; root slice pds-w1-crown-proof). Every later phase appends here — someone opening this mid-wave sees exactly where the wave stands. Phase: STRATEGIZE (surveying). Charter: .claude/workflows/bp-pds-charter.md. Prior wave Paper: pds-wave-20-2026-07-21.

Where this wave stands
STRATEGIZE done. 16 broad surveyors about to fly. The wave's whole worth: spend the budget on DIAGNOSIS, never on a guess. The crown is 9/12; one crown attempt remains (5/6 spent). Outcome is binary and both branches are wins: crown SEALED 12/12 by a clean re-fire, or a NAMED, evidenced refusal that files the real api bug for a felix wave.

The Wish

THIS CYCLE: diagnose rung 1, then fire the last attempt. Wave 20 finally FIRED the crown at the derived 897 MiB floor (the fossil 2200 is gone). It got 6 PASS but rung 1 (the import) FAILED with a Postgres 25P02 aborted-transaction. ONE attempt remains (5/6). Diagnose the root of the tx abort — do NOT burn the last attempt on a guess — then fire clean. Root task: pds-w1-crown-proof.

Where Wave 20 Left It — the win, and the fail

THE WIN (do not relitigate): wave 20 derived the floor to 897 MiB (PDS-D276/D277, mutation-proven; both launcher knobs + harness cond_b; frozen blob e219e97c untouched) on branch loop-epic/arm-the-launcher-at-the-derived-897-floo-0 (commit c4569f98e, PUSHED). It FIRED on draw 1 in the box's real ~1361 MiB regime: 6 PASS (0a, 0b, 0c, 3, 7, 8), 4 ABORT (2/4/5 wait on rung 1), 1 FAIL, attempts 4->5. The fossil-floor wall is permanently gone. That is not this wave's problem.

THE FAIL — rung 1 (STEP 1, the pull), classified ENGINE-FAIL not harness bug. The SOURCE export was clean (exit 0, 76,442,112 bytes, 34 blobs). The IMPORT into the SCRATCH target 500'd. Scratch log for request_id GMRmnzN-yl-UNAkAAABk: Sent 500 in 15052ms, then (Postgrex.Error) ERROR 25P02 (in_failed_sql_transaction) current transaction is aborted... query: SET session_replication_role = DEFAULT.

The 25P02 is a MASK, not the root
SET session_replication_role = DEFAULT is the trigger/FK re-enable at import END. It failed only because an EARLIER statement already aborted the transaction. The true root is that first-failing statement, which the visible log line does not show. The import ran 15s before aborting. Every diagnostic move this wave makes is aimed at that first-failing statement.

The load-bearing surprise the strategy turns on

The proof harness itself (scripts/pds-pull-proof.sh:439 and :919) already KNOWS that clean-mode import 500s a 25P02 on a populated target, at workspace_bundle.ex:233 — and it uses --merge SPECIFICALLY to avoid that. Yet wave 20 used --merge --with-blobs and STILL got the 25P02. Merge mode is DESIGNED to converge on a populated target (PDS-D8, 17/17 green). So a merge-path 25P02 is genuinely surprising, and the naive inference 'dirty scratch => hypothesis (a), just re-fire' is NOT airtight. That surprise is why the diagnosis must READ the abort, not assume it.

The Direction — Read the Abort, Then Fire

The finished experience: the epic's 15-wave crown is either SEALED 12/12 or REFUSED with a named, evidenced api bug — and in EITHER case the wave never guessed. The wave spends its budget on DIAGNOSIS, not on the last attempt. Concretely, the diagnosis is TWO complementary moves, both of which spend ZERO crown attempts:

MOVE 1 — CAPTURE THE ROOT. The wave-20 scratch target is still alive; the scratch API stayed HTTP 200 after the fail (the tx rolled back cleanly). Enable statement-level error logging on the scratch Postgres (log_min_error_statement / log_statement) and re-run the EXACT failing import against it — no crown attempt is spent — to surface the FIRST-failing SQL statement the 25P02 masks. This is the ground truth the whole wave turns on: a named statement, not an inference.

MOVE 2 — SORT ON A CLEAN SCRATCH. Boot a GUARANTEED-fresh scratch from CURRENT origin/main (D34/D54 traps: CC=/usr/bin/clang, no auto deps.get, BARKPARK_HOME under 85 chars, redirect not pipe, mint admin token, ~3.5min cold, budget an OOM without chasing it), then run the identical export --profile dev --dataset production --with-blobs piped to import default --yes --merge --with-blobs in ISOLATION (reuse the 76MB artifact if still present, else a fresh scoped/cheap export). Booting fresh from current origin/main removes BOTH dirty-data collisions (a) AND schema/migration skew (c) at once.

The sort
Clean isolation PASS (and MOVE 1 named a state/schema cause a fresh boot demonstrably removes) => it was (a)/(c). FIX = fresh scratch; the crown's own step 1 pulls into a fresh empty-shell. PROCEED to fire. Same 25P02 on a fresh scratch => the merge-with-blobs handler has a real bug that blocks the crown itself. That is api/** — OUT of the scripts/pds-* fence. FILE it for a felix/api wave, record a NAMED REFUSAL. A named refusal is a win.

If PROCEED — fire the last attempt clean

Everything else is proven from wave 20. Re-cut the fire worktree at CURRENT origin/main (f76367999) so rung 0b's merge-base --is-ancestor DEPLOYED_SHA worktree_sha holds; checkout the floor-897 launcher from the branch into it (git -C <wt> checkout loop-epic/arm-the-launcher-at-the-derived-897-floo-0 -- scripts/pds-crown-launch.sh) while keeping worktree HEAD at origin/main for 0b. GUARANTEE a fresh scratch (the actual root fix for (a)) — archive the stale run dir (D269), confirm the launcher boots its own fresh target rather than reusing wave-18's leftover pointer. Re-derive the budget at L1 (attempts now 5, budget = spent+2 = 7). Arm detached, RETURN, do not poll. Collect is the LEAD's.

CRITICAL COORDINATION — re-freeze the merge window
The lead LIFTED the merge freeze after wave-20's climb died (to drain 25 PRs). Before ARMING the last attempt the lead must RE-FREEZE. The protected window is fire-worktree-cut -> fire: no merge may reach origin/main in that window, because a merge triggers a guerrilla redeploy that moves DEPLOYED_SHA ahead of the worktree and INVALIDATES rung 0b mid-climb — that was precisely the wave-18 failure. Coordinate via this Paper: state the exact moment 0b must be protected, and the lead holds merges until fire.

Direction Debate — the rivals weighed

RIVAL A (WINNER) — Diagnose-then-fire with a TWO-MOVE diagnosis (capture the masked statement + clean-scratch isolation). Both moves are free of crown attempts; together they discriminate (a)/(c) from (b) airtight.

RIVAL B — Assume (a); skip the diagnostic; just make the launcher boot a guaranteed-fresh scratch and fire. LOSES: the wish explicitly forbids guessing, and the merge-path 25P02 surprise (above) means (b) is a live possibility. If it is (b) or a (c) a fresh boot does not fix, attempt 6 is gone forever. The diagnostic spends ZERO attempts, so it is free insurance against losing the epic's last shot. The asymmetry is total.

RIVAL C — Fix the merge-import-with-blobs handler now for real. LOSES to the fence: api/** is OUT of scripts/pds-*; a handler fix needs a felix/api wave with a protective test (the 25P02-masking / per-member savepoint honesty is PDS-D18 backlog). If (b), we FILE, we do not fix.

RIVAL D — Widen the crown (re-derive more rungs / relax criteria). LOSES: the endgame is narrow — unblock rung 1. Wave 20 already proved 6 rungs. Widening dilutes the single remaining attempt.

Sharpest attack on the winner, and how the wave absorbs it

ATTACK: a clean isolation PASS does not guarantee the real fire passes — the isolation might reuse the stale 76MB artifact or a subtly different import, while the real fire's FRESH export hits a source-side CHECK constraint (D32) or schema drift the isolation never exercised. So a green isolation is a false all-clear and attempt 6 still dies.

ABSORBED: (1) the isolation mirrors the real fire's step-1 command EXACTLY (same export --profile dev --dataset production --with-blobs then import --merge --with-blobs) against a scratch booted from CURRENT origin/main — the same schema the fire's scratch carries. (2) MOVE 1 independently NAMES the true root, so we know whether it was state/schema/handler, not merely 'it passed this time'. (3) The fire's own rungs 0a/0b/0c and the D32/D47 schema-migration parity re-prove the source-sha and CHECK conditions at L1 — the source-side path is gated by the crown's own preflight, not by the isolation. Diagnosis discriminates the handler; the crown preflight covers the source.

The Survey Plan — 16 broad assignments

Width is cheap now; the Digest phase distills. Each surveyor answers one concrete question and reports to its own bp task; the next Fable folds them here. Questions and why each matters:

scratch-alive

Q: Is the wave-20 scratch target still ALIVE and reachable? Its port, BARKPARK_HOME, and pointer file (/tmp/pds-scratch.pds-w14.c7528814.last vs /tmp/pds-scratch-target.last). Can we re-run the exact failing import against it and read its Postgres log for request_id GMRmnzN-yl-UNAkAAABk? Files: pds-scratch-target.sh, /tmp/pds-scratch*.

Why: MOVE 1 needs a live target and a readable PG log to capture the first-failing statement.

What is the EXACT wave-20 import command (finding: cloud workspace import default --yes --merge --with-blobs against the scratch API)?

Why: This is the decisive diagnostic; it must be executable within the scripts/pds-* fence.

Which SECONDARY unique indexes could a dirty scratch collide on that ON CONFLICT(pk) will NOT catch? D8/D9/D73, workspace_bundle.ex:233.

DEBRIEF — Review (2026-07-21)

Wave 21 outcome: diagnosis delivered, fire NOT armed, one-shot PRESERVED The wave delivered the hard half of the wish — the rung-1 abort is diagnosed to ground truth (verdict (a) DIRTY-SCRATCH, proven end-to-end) — and correctly did NOT deliver the easy-but-dangerous half. What shipped

PART A DONE and proves the wish's diagnostic mandate to ground truth: a guaranteed-fresh scratch was booted under PDS_RUN_ID=pdsw21-iso at BARKPARK_HOME=/private/tmp/pds-w21iso.a512 (up --verify -> PASS, GET /api/schemas 200, server :20142, empty migrated DB), and the EXACT rung-1 import that 500'd with 25P02 against the dirty wave-18 target imported CLEAN into it: exit 0, receipt content_edges=5109 / total_rows=15915 / 34 blobs 0 failed; post-import DB confirmed content_edges=5109, documents=3602. /tmp/pds-full-export/attempts stayed 5 — ZERO crown attempts spent on the diagnosis. During the build, origin/main advanced to d633786 (four tasks-only commits #5535-#5538 merged). Guerrilla auto-deploys on merge, so guerrilla live HEAD is now d633786.
